# frostmoln_appgw_backend_pool (Resource)

Manages a backend pool on a Frostmoln Application Gateway: a set of backends sharing a protocol, a load-balancing algorithm and a health check.

The backend pool API has no update operation, so every attribute forces a new resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "frostmoln_appgw_backend_pool" "web" {
  gateway_id = frostmoln_application_gateway.edge.id
  name       = "web"
  protocol   = "http"
  algorithm  = "round_robin"
}

# Re-encrypt to the backend. tls_verify_backend is left to the platform default
# unless you have a reason: setting it to false silently disables certificate
# verification.
resource "frostmoln_appgw_backend_pool" "api" {
  gateway_id = frostmoln_application_gateway.edge.id
  name       = "api"
  protocol   = "https"

  tls_verify_backend = true
  tls_server_name    = "api.internal"
  tls_ca_certificate = file("${path.module}/internal-ca.pem")

  session_affinity    = "cookie"
  session_cookie_name = "FMSESSION"

  timeout_connect_ms  = 2000
  timeout_response_ms = 30000
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `gateway_id` (String) The Application Gateway this pool belongs to.
- `name` (String) The name of the pool.

### Optional

- `algorithm` (String) How requests are distributed: `round_robin`, `least_connections` or `source_ip`.
- `protocol` (String) How the gateway talks to the backends: `http` or `https`. `https` re-encrypts traffic on the way to the backend.
- `session_affinity` (String) Pin a client to one backend: `none`, `cookie` or `source_ip`.
- `session_cookie_name` (String) The cookie used for affinity. Required when `session_affinity` is `cookie`.
- `timeout_connect_ms` (Number) Connect timeout in milliseconds.
- `timeout_response_ms` (Number) Response timeout in milliseconds.
- `tls_ca_certificate` (String) PEM CA bundle used to verify backend certificates.
- `tls_server_name` (String) The server name presented to the backend (SNI) and verified against its certificate.
- `tls_verify_backend` (Boolean) Verify the backend's certificate on an `https` pool.

Leave this unset to keep the platform default. It is deliberately **not** defaulted to `false` here: sending an explicit `false` for a practitioner who never mentioned it would silently disable certificate verification.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) The creation timestamp.
- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the backend pool.
- `updated_at` (String) The last update timestamp.
